issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may reverse a refusal to reject a plaint when allowing the rejection application would finally dispose of the suit.
material_facts: The trial court dismissed an application seeking rejection of the plaint.
The defendant challenged that order before the District Court in revision.
Allowing the application and rejecting the plaint would finally dispose of the suit.
The suit was instituted before the later amendment to the applicable state revision provision.
issues.conclusion: The District Court had jurisdiction to allow the application and reject the plaint, and the High Court was wrong to hold otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 115 as amended in the state, a revisional court may vary or reverse an order where doing so would finally dispose of the suit. The Court relied on Pandurang Dhondi Chougule v. Maruti Hari Jadhav, which explains the limits of revisional jurisdiction, and Tek Singh v. Shashi Verma, which addresses revisions against interlocutory orders.

predicates.revision_proceeding: A party sought review by revision of an order made by a subordinate court.
predicates.revision_challenges_refusal_to_end_suit: The challenged order refused an application that, if allowed, would terminate the suit.
predicates.allowing_challenge_would_finally_end_sui: Reversing the challenged order would bring the suit to an end.

issues.definition: When a revision challenges a refusal to end a suit and allowing the challenge would end it, the revisional court may reverse the order.

issues.legal_issue: An aggrieved party may seek supervisory review when a revisional court rejects a plaint, even though rejection of a plaint is a decree.
material_facts: The District Court, acting as a revisional court, allowed the application to reject the plaint.
The plaintiff challenged that rejection by filing a petition under the Constitution's supervisory jurisdiction.
The rejection had not been made by the trial court exercising original jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: A supervisory petition was available to challenge rejection of the plaint by the revisional court; if the trial court had rejected it, an appeal from the decree would have been available instead.
issues.legal_principle: Rejection of a plaint is a decree under Section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, and a decree made by a court exercising original jurisdiction is appealable under Section 96. Where rejection is made by a revisional court, the aggrieved party may seek relief under Article 227 of the Constitution.

predicates.challenge_to_rejection_in_revision: The proceeding challenges a decision rejecting a plaint in revision.
predicates.plaint_rejected_by_revisional_court: A revisional court, rather than the trial court exercising original jurisdiction, rejected the plaint.
predicates.aggrieved_party_seeks_review: A party adversely affected by the rejection seeks review of that decision.

issues.definition: If a revisional court rejects a plaint and an affected party challenges that rejection, supervisory review is available.

issues.legal_issue: A plaint that, read as a whole and taken at face value, discloses a real cause of action cannot be rejected for failure to disclose a cause of action.
material_facts: The plaint alleged that the plaintiff gave a cheque to an advocate as security under an agreement, subject to the defendant fulfilling an undertaking.
The plaint alleged that the defendant failed to fulfil that undertaking, the cheque was handed over contrary to the agreement, and the cheque was dishonoured after presentation.
The defendant sought rejection of the plaint, including on the ground that it disclosed no cause of action.
issues.conclusion: The plaint disclosed a cause of action on its face and could not be rejected on the ground that it failed to disclose one.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the plaint must be read as a whole, with its averments taken as true for this purpose. The Court relied on T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, Azhar Hussain v. Rajiv Gandhi, Sopan Sukhdeo Sable v. Assistant Charity Commissioner, I.T.C. Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal, Liverpool & London S.P. & I Assn. Ltd. v. M.V. Sea Success I, Madanuri Sri Rama Chandra Murthy v. Syed Jalal, Dahiben v. Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali, Rajendra Bajoria v. Hemant Kumar Jalan, Hardesh Ores (P.) Ltd. v. Hede & Co., D. Ramachandran v. R.V. Janakiraman, and Saleem Bhai v. State of Maharashtra.

predicates.application_to_reject_plaint: A party applied for the plaint in a suit to be rejected at the threshold.
predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.plaint_read_as_whole_discloses_real_caus: The plaint's averments, taken as true and read together, set out a real basis for seeking relief.

issues.definition: In a civil suit, a plaint that sets out a real basis for relief when read as a whole cannot be rejected for lack of a cause of action.

issues.legal_issue: Omission of further or consequential relief does not justify rejecting a declaratory plaint at the threshold when entitlement to the declaration has not yet been determined.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought declaratory reliefs without also seeking further consequential relief.
Whether the plaintiff was entitled to the declarations had not been decided.
The omission was raised as a ground for rejecting the plaint.
issues.conclusion: Whether further relief was required could be considered at final adjudication, and its omission did not justify rejecting the plaint at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act bars a declaration where a plaintiff able to seek further relief omits it. Whether further relief is required arises for consideration at final adjudication, because the need for such relief depends on whether the declaration is granted.

predicates.declaratory_civil_suit: The plaintiff has filed a civil suit seeking a declaration.
predicates.further_relief_omitted: The plaintiff has not also sought further relief that may accompany the declaration.
predicates.entitlement_to_declaration_not_yet_decid: The court has not yet determined whether the plaintiff is entitled to the declaration.

issues.definition: In a declaratory civil suit, omission of further relief does not warrant threshold rejection before entitlement to the declaration is decided.

issues.legal_issue: A civil suit seeking declarations that would in substance restrain another party from pursuing legal remedies, including criminal proceedings, is barred and its plaint may be rejected.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought declarations that a dishonoured cheque had been delivered only as security, had been handed over contrary to an agreement, and did not create liability to supply goods or pay the cheque amount.
The defendant had presented the cheque, it had been dishonoured, and the defendant had issued a notice under the law governing dishonoured cheques.
The Court found that the requested declarations would in substance prevent the defendant from pursuing available legal remedies, including prosecution or a recovery claim.
The plaintiff's grievances about breach of the agreement could be pursued through appropriate remedies and defences in law.
issues.conclusion: The declaratory reliefs were barred because they were, in substance, an attempt to restrain the defendant from pursuing legal remedies. The plaint was therefore liable to be rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 41(b) and 41(d) of the Specific Relief Act prohibit injunctions restraining proceedings in court and criminal matters. Sections 118(a) and 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act provide a rebuttable presumption of consideration for a negotiable instrument and address liability following dishonour of a cheque; the alleged absence of a legally enforceable liability may be raised in the appropriate proceeding. The Court relied on Cotton Corporation of India Ltd. v. United Industrial Bank Ltd., Ratna Commercial Enterprises Ltd. v. Vasutech Ltd., and the authorities discussed there, including Atul Kumar Singh v. Jalveen Rosha.

predicates.civil_suit_seeking_declarations_about_di: A plaintiff brings a civil suit seeking declarations about the effect or enforceability of a dishonoured cheque.
predicates.declarations_in_substance_would_block_an: The practical effect of the requested declarations would be to prevent another party from pursuing available legal remedies, including a criminal proceeding or a recovery claim.

issues.definition: A civil plaint seeking declarations about a dishonoured cheque must be rejected when those declarations would in substance block another party from pursuing legal remedies.
